#2728. Week 11 Preview: #1 Seed on the Line?

The Minnesota Vikings will travel to Mexico City to face the 8-1 San Francisco 49ers in a game that could very well determine the #1 seed in the NFC playoff bracket in January.

With the Vikings currently tied with the 7-2 Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears in the ridiculously good NFC North, a win over the 49ers could put them in the driver's seat for the rest of the way. After Sunday, the schedule gets much easier, with five of the final seven games at U.S. Bank Stadium. The Vikings also have the benefit of already being 3-1 in the division, with the final two at home. The Lions and Bears each have four division games left. And while the Packers may "just" be 6-4 and destined for last place, they're certainly no pushovers.

A loss to the 49ers certainly wouldn't dash the good guys' hopes for a division crown, as they'd still control their own destiny; it could, for all intents and purposes, slam the door on the coveted #1 seed in the NFC and its lone bye. The 49ers do have some tricky games left, but I'd think the only one they'd be underdogs in would be the Week 16 road game against the Kansas City Chiefs. At effectively two games behind, the Vikings would probably need to be flawless.

Kirk Cousins' return changes the formula dramatically. If the trade didn't happen, I'd give the Vikings offense little to no shot at hitting 20+ points here. Or maybe even 10. And this is with the knowledge that the 49ers defense is kind of living off its reputation a bit from the earlier Kyle Shanahan era.

Don't get me wrong, they're solid. But it's not the unit from the 2019-2022 Robert Saleh-DeMeco Ryans years. That said, new (and highly experienced) coordinator Raheem Morris has them playing well: 11th in points per game (21.8), 6th in total yards (308), 17th in pass yards allowed (226), 2nd in rush yards allowed (82.6), and 20th in 3rd-down conversion rate (41%).

The standout stat is their exceptional success so far at stopping the run. The Vikings average 108.6 per game (19th) but improved in both volume and efficiency last week with Cousins back – e.g., higher YPC (4.2) and seven rushing first downs. Avoiding 3rd-and-long situations will be crucial in this one. Nice gains on 1st and 2nd downs will also open up the play-action game, which I'm sure will be a focus for Kevin O'Connell. Keeping the 49ers defense on their toes will make an already average pass defense even less effective.

Many 49ers sites are focusing on the fact that Cousins already faced this defense a few weeks ago, and the results were…suboptimal: 216 yards, 1 TD, 3 INTs, and a 55.3 QBR. Does this matter? To a certain extent, I suppose. Does it mean history will repeat itself? Definitely not. Different play-caller, better offensive personnel, and almost certainly a more effective game plan, with that game on film to learn from. To be honest, I fully expect this to be a far more challenging unit to face than the Packers were a week prior.

If you're going to go there, it's only fair to point out that Cousins is 2-1 in regular-season games in a Vikings uniform against Shanahan's 49ers, averaging 286.7 yards passing in those games, with 6 TDs and 2 INTs for an overall passer rating of 99.4. One of those was a great home win in 2023, when he passed for 378 yards in a victory without Justin Jefferson against the then 5-2 49ers.

Again, all that aside, getting the running game going early in this one will be critical. Allowing Nick Bosa, Keion White, and company to go wild repeatedly on 3rd-and-long isn't ideal, even if the 49ers' overall pass-rush metrics (e.g., sack rate) this season have been at or below average.

Again, this is your main event of the evening. Strength vs. strength. The NFL's #1 scoring/EPA defense faces the #1 yardage/efficiency offense. We all know how historically dominant the Vikings' defense has been. I touched on it a few days ago. But with apologies to the Bills, Lions, and Bears, this will almost certainly be the season's biggest challenge.

The 49ers are formidable: 2nd in points per game (31.2), 1st in total yards (399.8), 7th in pass yards (255.8), 3rd in rush yards (144), and 1st in 3rd-down conversion rate (52%). The Vikings' rankings in those categories? 1st, 2nd, 2nd, 17th, and 3rd, respectively.

The number that stands out to Vikings fans is that we're 17th in rushing yards allowed per game. There are vulnerabilities, no doubt. This is especially true since it's no secret that Christian McCaffrey is the straw that stirs the drink for the 49ers offense. He's Brock Purdy's security blanket and among the most dangerous dual threats in the NFL. But digging a bit deeper into the numbers, I found that the Vikings are much better (7th) in run EPA/play, at around -0.10. That makes you feel a bit better, but the eye test (for me, anyway) shows the concerns are legitimate.

If the Vikings are effective at stopping the run on early downs, it will play right into our hands. What's unique about Flores' scheme is that it flips traditional schematic reasoning on its head. Logic would dictate that the more aggressive the defense, the more vulnerable a team becomes in the quick, on-time passing game. Instead, the Vikings did a good job of taking that away in the last matchup against Purdy and the 49ers in 2024. ESPN's Jason McCourty and Dan Orlovsky had a great discussion about it that's worth your time.

And here's another post from The Athletic's Alec Lewis that's just ridiculous.

In the end, Kyle Shanahan is 0-5 when Brian Flores is on the opposing sideline, whether as a head coach or a coordinator. 49ers fans will say he's due. It's only a matter of time. Vikings fans will counter that this is the best Flores unit Shanahan has ever faced. Who will be right? We shall see.

The unique wildcard here is the altitude issue in Mexico City and which team's differing methods will prove more effective. I'm not a biologist and have no clue which strategy is better. I'm sure there's science supporting both approaches; why would a team deliberately put itself at such a disadvantage?

What I do know is that after Week 1, the 49ers had the oldest average roster in the NFL (27.49 years). They've since traded for 34-year-old Keenan Allen and 32-year-old DeForest Buckner to play prominent roles. The Vikings have similar issues, specifically with Harrison Smith (37) and Kyle Van Noy (35). You can also note Kirk Cousins (38). But there's a fundamental difference between a quarterback taking three- and five-step drops and a receiver running routes and blocking all game. The same goes for an interior lineman battling in the trenches for four quarters. Depth and scheme comfort/familiarity on both sides of the ball will be important here. Expect more varied snap counts than usual after this one.

I'm cautiously optimistic about this game. Jordan Addison being out again isn't ideal, but it opens opportunities for a Jauan Jennings revenge game, and Myles Price and Tai Felton played well last week, too. The key for Cousins will be to avoid turnovers, and the way to do that is not to press, which I felt was a bit of an issue on his return last week. The interception that counted was one example, and the one that didn't, because his knee was fortunately down, was another. If he takes what's there, nothing more and nothing less, the Vikings offense will be fine. The name of the game is to keep the chains moving and to afford the defense time to recover. Unless there's an unexpected turnover barrage, whoever wins time of possession is likely the victor. That's always true, but it's even more critical given the atmospheric conditions.

On defense, it all comes down to scheming effective pressure on Purdy without committing more than five too often. Listen, Flores is going to bring the heat, but it wouldn't shock me if the blitz rate were slightly reduced from the record-breaking highs if it's not getting home early. Purdy isn't going to be easily rattled and, with time, will quickly make the proper reads to exploit the mid-15 to 20-yard range, where we can sometimes be susceptible. And, of course, having to account for McCaffrey, who can take it to the house from anywhere, on every play could even out the numbers game.

I've got a death grip on the positive vibes since Cousins' return, and I have no plans to let go until the situation warrants it. I want that bye week, and I think we'll stay on track to get it.

The NFC North continues to perform like no other division in the league.

Three of the teams (Lions, Bears, Vikings) have a record of 7-2 through 10 weeks. The Packers are 6-4.

#2724. ‘Isn’t Even Better Than Kyrie Irving,’ ‘Trying To Keep His Job’ — NBA Fans Troll Kenny Atkinson Over James Harden Top-10 Claim

James Harden turned back the clock on Friday night, pouring in 51 points to lift the Cleveland Cavaliers past the Indiana Pacers 128-119 at Rocket Arena. After watching the 37-year-old guard pass Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history, head coach Kenny Atkinson took his praise to an unexpected level.

Atkinson made a strong case for Harden's place among the NBA's all-time greats during his postgame press conference, a comment that quickly drew mockery across social media.

Cleveland led 62-61 at halftime, with Harden already at 24 points, before erupting for 43 in the third quarter. Harden scored 18 of them, including 13 during a 21-4 run that helped the Cavs build a 105-83 lead heading into the fourth. Indiana cut the deficit to six late, but Harden scored 7 of Cleveland's final 9 points to close it out.

He finished 15-for-26 from the floor, hit seven 3-pointers and went 14-for-14 at the line, adding 6 rebounds and 6 assists in 40 minutes. It was his highest-scoring game as a Cavalier and his 26th career 50-point outing, trailing only Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Atkinson urged everyone not to take the 18-year veteran for granted.

"Guy's special. We gotta, I know, you know, everyone wants a perfect, but we gotta appreciate this guy," Atkinson said. "You know, like, this guy is top 10 of all time. I know I appreciate every day coaching him. It's an honor. I really mean that. Doesn't happen to a lot of coaches to get to coach a guy like that."

The comment didn't sit well with everyone. One fan summed up the immediate disbelief, posting, "Top what??" along with a reaction meme.

Another wondered if the Cavaliers coach simply misspoke, asking, "Top 10 for guards right? Not like all time in general?"

Others went straight after Harden's comparisons with his peers. One user bluntly wrote, "Isn't even better than Kyrie Irving."

Irving is a nine-time All-Star and an NBA champion, while Harden has the edge in individual accolades, including the 2018 MVP award and a place on the NBA 75th Anniversary Team.

Sports radio host Brendan Tobin joined the jokes, taking a sarcastic jab at Atkinson: "Let's give it up for Coach analytically we're up 3-1, everybody."

Even fans who acknowledged Harden's big night refused to accept the top-10 label without a fight.

"TOP 10 Of all time FOR WHAT CHOKING??? 😂😂😂. (Fairs tho Harden was amazing today)"

Harden's playoff reputation remains a point of contention, particularly after Cleveland's postseason disappointment last year. The Cavaliers were swept 4-0 by the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals, with Harden committing 84 turnovers across 18 playoff games.

Harden's career résumé certainly carries weight. He has won the 2018 MVP award, claimed three scoring titles, earned 11 All-Star selections and made the NBA 75th Anniversary Team. He also ranks ninth on the all-time scoring list and second in career 3-pointers, behind only Stephen Curry.

SEE ALSO: 'I Didn't Know Steph Curry Was Gonna Be One of the Greatest Shooters in the World' – Dwight Howard Reveals Major 'Regret' From His NBA Career

Harden also entered Friday's game averaging 16.2 ppg on the season, with 7, 11 and 9 points in three of his previous six appearances.

Meanwhile, with Cleveland sitting at 9-8 and Harden averaging 18.4 points and 6.3 assists through 16 games, one viewer suggested Atkinson had an ulterior motive for the over-the-top praise.

Atkinson, the 2025 Coach of the Year, faced speculation about his job security during last season's playoffs.

The Cavaliers will look to build on the win when they visit the Chicago Bulls on Monday.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

#2719. Knee surgery complicates Puka Nacua's future

On Friday, Rams coach Sean McVay said receiver Puka Nacua will miss “a couple months.” Nacua is reportedly expected to miss a couple months more than that.

Via ESPN, the recovery time following surgery to repair the MCL tear is four to five months. If accurate, that ends Nacua’s 2026 season.

The problem becomes 2027. Nacua is in the last year of his rookie contract. He hasn’t gotten a second deal, due in large part to the off-field issues that recently resulted in a three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy and that culminated in an offseason stay at an in-patient holistic rehab facility after he was “drowning myself” in alcohol.

Based on the ESPN report, Nacua won’t be back to 100 percent before free agency starts. The Rams will have to decide whether to sign him to a new deal, to apply the franchise tag (or the transition tag), or to let him become a free agent.

The injury makes it very difficult for Nacua to land in the Jaxon Smith-Njigba ballpark ($42.15 million per year), even though Nacua’s skills and abilities justify that type of deal.

The situation becomes a prime example of the extent to which off-field issues can complicate a player’s financial interests. Without the New Year’s Eve incident that resulted in a lawsuit and, eventually, a diversion program and, inevitably, a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua would have had his second contract by now. Or, at a minimum, he would have had greater standing to hold out (or hold in) until he got paid what he deserves.

Instead, Nacua continued to carry the injury risk into the final year of his rookie contract. And the injury risk became reality 13 days ago, when McVay dialed up a running play to Nacua on third and 11 while trying to run out the clock in a 20-13 game against the Commanders.

It’s a win for the Rams, who may be able to keep Nacua for a lot less than it would cost to give him a market-level contract. However the Rams play the situation, Nacua’s knee injury will make it easier, and cheaper, to re-sign him.

Ultimately, Nacua may have to prove in 2027 that he is back to full strength. And he may have to get through a full season unscathed to unlock the long-term deal his performances earned — but his off-field complications squandered.

Given the way he plays, it’s hardly a given that Nacua will emerge from the 2027 season with the kind of performance, and health, that will finally get him the contract he should have gotten by now.

The New York Knicks nearly let a massive lead slip away against the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday night, but Mikal Bridges made sure it didn't cost them.

The Knicks appeared to be cruising early, pouring in 40 points in the first quarter and building a lead that grew to as many as 26. New York took a 66-43 advantage into halftime, but Portland roared back in the second half, outscoring the Knicks 53-31 over the final two quarters.

The defending champions knocked down 19 3-pointers on the night, yet the offense went cold after the break and allowed the Blazers to chip away at the deficit.

The men in black capped their comeback with a 12-0 run late in the fourth quarter to take a 96-94 lead, stunning the home crowd. With the clock winding down, the ball found Bridges, who calmly knocked down the game-winning triple to send the Garden into a frenzy.

It wasn't the first time Bridges has broken Portland's heart. Back in March 2025, he hit a buzzer-beating 3-pointer in overtime to give the Knicks a 114-113 victory over the Blazers.

Bridges finished with 12 points on an efficient 5-of-8 shooting, along with three assists and a steal. Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 30 points, knocking down six 3-pointers, while Landry Shamet scored 20 points, also hitting six triples. Andre Drummond grabbed 13 rebounds.

Donovan Clingan was a force for Portland, finishing with 22 points and 13 rebounds on 9-of-11 shooting. Deni Avdija added 20 points, nine rebounds and five assists, while Damian Lillard chipped in 15 points and Jrue Holiday filled up the stat sheet with 13 points, nine rebounds and seven assists.

With the victory, the Knicks extended their winning streak to four games and improved to 10-6 on the season. It was far from their cleanest performance, but thanks to Bridges, New York escaped with a win it nearly let slip away.

Although space at the apex appeared tight as the McLaren occupied the racing line, stewards determined Hamilton left the track and gained a lasting advantage, imposing a 10-second time penalty.

In a team radio message not broadcast on the global feed, Hamilton expressed clear frustration with the severity of the sanction.

"Isn't that interesting? One race where someone won't have it, and they'll be mitigating circumstances; they give them five seconds, they give me 10 for avoiding an incident," Hamilton told his race engineer.

Hamilton did not name a specific driver or grand prix in his message, yet his reference to "mitigating circumstances" and a reduced five-second penalty immediately recalled a recent flashpoint inside his own team.

Three weeks earlier at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November, Leclerc completed an off-track pass on Hamilton at Turn 4 on the opening lap. Under Formula 1's driving standards guidelines, leaving the track and gaining an advantage carries a standard 10-second penalty. In Mexico, however, the stewards halved Leclerc's sanction to five seconds, explicitly citing mitigation.

"The baseline penalty guideline is 10 seconds; however, in mitigation is the fact that car 44 was also off track on the inside of car 16 and this occurred early in the first lap," the FIA stewards wrote in their Mexico City decision.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari

That ruling sparked debate across the paddock at the time. Hamilton - who had served a 10-second penalty for a similar off-track offence in Mexico in 2025 - argued over team radio during the race that the lesser penalty failed to offset the clean-air benefit of staying ahead, while eventual race winner Max Verstappen also remarked afterwards that "normally, that penalty is 10 seconds, and now suddenly it's five".

From a regulatory standpoint, the two rulings hinge on context: stewards routinely apply greater leniency to crowded opening-lap incidents than to mid-race battles, where the full 10-second guideline remains the default.

Still, Hamilton's Las Vegas radio comments prove there is lingering driver frustration over how flexibly those guidelines are applied from weekend to weekend - a sore point the FIA hopes to ease when it begins phasing in full-time Formula 1 stewards in 2027.

#2711. Rams WR Puka Nacua reportedly out 4-5 months following knee surgery, will be sidelined for playoffs

While the Los Angeles Rams try to make the most of a 2026 campaign that began with astronomical expectations, wide receiver Puka Nacua is already working toward 2027. He had MCL surgery on Tuesday, and his recovery timeline is considered to be four to five months, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Saturday night.

Based on that reported prognosis, the 25-year-old Nacua will miss the remainder of the regular season and the playoffs.

The two-time All-Pro wideout received recommendations from three doctors to undergo the procedure, per ESPN's latest report, which noted that team doctor Neal ElAttrache performed the operation.

When the NFL announced this week that it was suspending Nacua three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, it reportedly wasn't aware that he had already had surgery.

The Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve with knee and turf toe injuries on Nov. 12, a week before the NFL imposed its suspension. Like any player who lands on IR, Nacua had to sit out four games before he could return. By the time the suspension was announced, the length of that ban and his remaining time on IR were aligned.

While that situation understandably turned heads, it's worth noting that Nacua isn't the first player to serve a suspension while on IR.

The last year has been a head-scratching one for Nacua, who's among the best wide receivers in the sport but has run into off-field trouble.

This past offseason, news broke that a woman was suing Nacua. She alleged that, on Dec. 31, 2025, he made an antisemitic statement and later bit her on the shoulder. Nacua's attorney denied the woman's claim that he made such a comment and downplayed the biting as "horseplay."

Nacua voluntarily entered a holistic care facility in March to focus on his personal growth. He reflected on that experience in May.

In seven games this season, Nacua — the league's 2025 receptions leader — piled up 70 catches for 715 yards and 4 touchdowns. He also scored on the ground once for a 6-4 Rams team that's hardly had the start it envisioned this fall.

Nacua's injuries occurred on the final offensive snap of L.A.'s Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders. He's in the last year of his rookie contract.

His future in L.A. has yet to be determined, and he won't be available for the Rams in the short term. That said, the Rams are hoping to get veteran wide receiver Davante Adams back down the stretch, as they make a push for the playoffs.

#2703. Josh Allen is one score away from four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns

Bills quarterback Josh Allen has become something that few quarterbacks are — a rushing-touchdown machine.

In nine 2026 games, Allen has 11 rushing touchdowns. With only one more, he’ll have his fourth straight season with 12 or more rushing touchdowns.

Via NBC Sports research, that would make him only the fifth player in NFL history to have four straight seasons with 12 or more rushing touchdowns.

The others were all running backs. LaDainian Tomlinson did it six times. Shaun Alexander accomplished it five times. Derrick Henry and Adrian Peterson did it four times each.

Henry, who has 10 this year, is two short of running his own streak to five seasons in a row.

Allen’s next rushing touchdown will give him 91 for his career, putting him in a tie for 12th all time with Franco Harris and Jerome Bettis. Given that Allen is only in his ninth season, the all-time rushing-touchdown record of 164, held my Emmitt Smith, could eventually be in jeopardy.

#2702. Clippers Fade Late Again in Dallas as Their Fourth-Quarter Problem Grows

The Clippers got the game right where they wanted it with a little more than five minutes to go Saturday night in Dallas, then watched it slip away again in a 110-100 loss to the Mavericks at American Airlines Center.

Kris Dunn hit a corner 3-pointer that cut the Dallas lead to 91-88 with 5:12 remaining, but the Mavericks answered with an 11-0 run helped along by two Clippers turnovers, and the visitors never threatened again. Kyrie Irving opened the night 1 of 7 from the field and still finished with 25 points, scoring 12 of them in the fourth quarter to close it out.

The loss dropped the Clippers to 4-11 overall and 0-7 on the road, and they have now lost three in a row since a home loss to Utah on Tuesday.

Brook Lopez sparked an early 9-0 burst, and the Clippers led 26-23 after one quarter before the second quarter went sideways on them. Dallas ripped off a 13-0 run in that period, won the quarter 29-18 and took a 52-44 lead into halftime.

The Clippers pushed back with a 30-point third quarter and trimmed the gap to 78-74 heading into the fourth, which set up the same closing stretch that has haunted this group all month. Dallas won the final period 32-26, and the Clippers finished with 16 turnovers that the Mavericks turned into 22 points.

Cooper Flagg had 22 points and eight assists for Dallas even though he went 7 of 13 at the free-throw line, the first time last season's Rookie of the Year has missed six free throws in a game. Walter Clayton Jr. added 16 points off the bench, Max Christie scored 13 and Daniel Gafford posted 10 points and 10 rebounds while the Dallas reserves outscored the Clippers' bench 42-35. The Mavericks played without starting forward P.J. Washington Jr., who sat out with an illness.

Nov 21, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; LA Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) looks to move the ball past Dallas Mavericks forward Daniel Gafford (21) during the second half at the American Airlines Center.

Nov 21, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; LA Clippers center Brook Lopez (11) looks to move the ball past Dallas Mavericks forward Daniel Gafford (21) during the second half at the American Airlines Center.

Lopez led the Clippers with 21 points, scoring 17 of them after halftime to keep his team within reach through the third quarter. Rui Hachimura added 19 points and made four 3-pointers to match his season high.

Darius Garland had 12 of his 16 points by halftime but went quiet after the break. The rest of the rotation had a hard time finding the basket, with Derrick Jones Jr. going 1 of 7 and Keaton Wagler going 1 of 8 as the Clippers shot 38.4% from the field and 15 of 45 from deep.

The Clippers were again without Bradley Beal, who is managing his right knee, along with Brandon Ingram and Jordan Miller.

I have watched this team hang around long enough to make things interesting and then come apart once the game asks for some composure, and it has happened far too many times this month. The Clippers led Utah 62-58 at halftime on Tuesday and lost by 25 after the Jazz poured in 44 points in the fourth quarter. They stayed with San Antonio deep into Thursday night before the Spurs won the final period 32-24, and Saturday in Dallas followed the same script.

Across the three games of this losing streak, opponents have outscored the Clippers 108-71 in fourth quarters, which is a gap that points at focus and execution far more than talent.

What bothers me most is who is on the floor when it happens. Lopez, Garland, Dunn, Hachimura and Jones have all played in big games in this league, and veterans with that much experience should be the ones who settle things down late and get a stop when the other side makes its push. Instead, the late turnovers keep piling up, the defense keeps breaking down in the final minutes, and the hole in the standings gets deeper with every loss.

Ingram is set to return Monday, and his ability to create his own shot late in games is exactly what this offense has been missing during these collapses. One player cannot fix a habit the whole group has fallen into, though, and the veterans in that locker room have to start owning the closing minutes before this season gets away from them.

The Clippers continue their road trip Monday at Houston, with tipoff set for 5:30 p.m. PT at Toyota Center.

#2700. Knee surgery complicates Puka Nacua's future

On Friday, Rams coach Sean McVay said receiver Puka Nacua will miss "a couple months." Nacua is reportedly expected to miss a couple months more than that.

Via ESPN, the recovery time following surgery to repair the MCL tear is four to five months. If accurate, that ends Nacua's 2026 season.

The problem becomes 2027. Nacua is in the last year of his rookie contract. He hasn't gotten a second deal, due in large part to the off-field issues that recently resulted in a three-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy and that culminated in an offseason stay at an in-patient holistic rehab facility after he was "drowning myself" in alcohol.

Based on the ESPN report, Nacua won't be back to 100 percent before free agency starts. The Rams will have to decide whether to sign him to a new deal, to apply the franchise tag (or the transition tag), or to let him become a free agent.

The injury makes it very difficult for Nacua to land in the Jaxon Smith-Njigba ballpark ($42.15 million per year), even though Nacua's skills and abilities justify that type of deal.

The situation becomes a prime example of the extent to which off-field issues can complicate a player's financial interests. Without the New Year's Eve incident that resulted in a lawsuit and, eventually, a diversion program and, inevitably, a suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy, Nacua would have had his second contract by now. Or, at a minimum, he would have had greater standing to hold out (or hold in) until he got paid what he deserves.

Instead, Nacua continued to carry the injury risk into the final year of his rookie contract. And the injury risk became reality 13 days ago, when McVay dialed up a running play to Nacua on third and 11 while trying to run out the clock in a 20-13 game against the Commanders.

It's a win for the Rams, who may be able to keep Nacua for a lot less than it would cost to give him a market-level contract. However the Rams play the situation, Nacua's knee injury will make it easier, and cheaper, to re-sign him.

Ultimately, Nacua may have to prove in 2027 that he is back to full strength. And he may have to get through a full season unscathed to unlock the long-term deal his performances earned — but his off-field complications squandered.

Given the way he plays, it's hardly a given that Nacua will emerge from the 2027 season with the kind of performance, and health, that will finally get him the contract he should have gotten by now.

#2699. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2694. Puka Nacua injury report is devastating news for Rams

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to miss the rest of the season, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Nacua underwent MCL surgery and it is expected to take him four to five months to fully recover.

He is currently on injured reserve, while also serving a three-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy.

More: NFL puts product over principles with Puka Nacua suspension | Opinion

Injuries have plagued the Rams this season and this news might be their worst yet.

Nacua had played in the season opener but was then sidelined several weeks due to a hip and groin injury. He returned in Week 4 but he hasn't played since Week 9 and now won't for the rest of the year.

Defensive tackle Poona Ford and kicker Blake Grupe are among the other players ruled out for the season for the Rams.

Fellow standout receiver Davante Adams suffered a hamstring injury in recent weeks and is not expected back until later this season. Myles Garrett also missed significant time after playing in the season opener before recently returning.

Nacua is unlikely to return for the season and the playoffs, if the Rams are able to qualify.

Los Angeles did not make a significant move before the trade deadline to bring in a receiver, leaving the Rams to count on receivers that have low production this season.

CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield will be asked to move forward as the primary receiving options for now with Nacua out of action and Adams still out.

Daniels has played in four games this season but has just one reception for 22 yards. He was a sixth round selection (No. 197 overall) out of Miami by the Rams in 2026.

Mumpfield has started three of the 10 games he's played in this season, producing 14 catches on 27 targets for 243 yards and a touchdown. He had not seen more than four targets in a game, outside of his four catches on eight targets during a game against the Denver Broncos on Sept. 27.

#2692. Lakers rookie makes most of biggest opportunity he’s gotten so far

Lakers coach JJ Redick has emphasized for weeks that every player on his roster is going to get an opportunity to play.

The nature of an 82-game regular season necessitates flexibility with playing rotations.

Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket. NBAE via Getty Images

During Friday's 106-104 home win over the Kings, rookie Cameron Carr got his most significant opportunity with the Lakers to date.

And his performance showed why he's deserving of more playing opportunities moving forward.

With Austin Reaves sidelined for the fourth consecutive game because of a bruised left heel, Carr was in the rotation off the bench, playing 11 minutes.

Unlike some of his previous playing time, a good amount of which has come when the game's results were already decided, the former Baylor Bear's minutes had a direct impact on the Lakers' chances of winning.

And the rookie made the playing time count, having five points on 2-for-5 shooting (1-for-4 on 3-pointers), a steal and a rebound.

"He looked great," Walker Kessler said. "He hit some big shots, played with physicality. He's got some long arms, I can tell you that. That layup he made — he's just got some long arms. He looked good tonight. I was happy. It was good to see."

Cameron Carr of the Los Angeles Lakers speaks to the media. NBAE via Getty Images

The stats don't matter as much as the comfort Carr showed when he was on the court.

He didn't hesitate to shoot the corner 3-pointer that momentarily gave the Lakers a two-point lead midway through the second quarter. And didn't shy away from contact on a layup later in the quarter.

Carr looked ready for the defensive physicality needed to hold his own on that end of the floor.

"That was huge," Quentin Grimes said. "I mean, as a rookie, you got to go out there and kind of earn minutes. Everybody kind of has to do that at one point some time in their career. And he got thrown in there, hit a big 3, hit a tough layup and had a couple good closeouts and got some stops. So, those are the things that earn trust from a coach when they throw you out there even more later in the season, for sure."

Redick has said Carr and second-year forward Adou Thiero's development over the next couple of years could raise the team's collective ceiling.

But before they can be ceiling-raisers, Carr and Thiero need to establish a floor for themselves.

Jaden Hardy #7 and Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers smile during a game against the Sacramento Kings. NBAE via Getty Images

With Reaves expected to make his return to the floor next week, playing time won't be available as it has been with him sidelined.

But Carr showed, at least for one game, he's ready to contribute more when his number is called.

And it's on the Lakers to find more chances for him so he can develop into the ceiling-raiser they're looking for him to be.

#2690. Matthew Stafford gets emotional about Puka Nacua’s surgery and human cost of football

Matthew Stafford has spent enough time in NFL training rooms to know there's a difference between playing through pain and gambling with your future.

So when the Rams quarterback learned that his favorite target, Puka Nacua, needed surgery to repair his injured right MCL, Stafford wasn't thinking about the passes they wouldn't complete together or the touchdowns left on the table.

He was thinking about his teammate's life and career moving forward.

Matthew Stafford (9) of the Los Angeles Rams interacts with teammate Puka Nacua (12) before an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 25, 2026. Getty Images

"I obviously hope all that is in the best interest of his long-term health because that's what I care about as a human being, and his future," Stafford said Saturday.

Nacua underwent surgery Tuesday, effectively ending his 2026 season, including any potential postseason run. His recovery is expected to take four to five months, with doctors anticipating he'll be healthy for the 2027 season.

For a Rams team already decimated by injuries, losing Nacua is another crushing blow. But Stafford understands the bigger picture.

"For a guy that puts a ton of effort into trying to be out there every single Sunday for us, he plays, you guys know, as violently as anybody in the NFL, especially at his position," Stafford said. "He puts his body on the line for us, and unfortunately, he had to get some things fixed and cleaned up."

Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates with Puka Nacua #12 after a touchdown pass against the Carolina Panthers on Jan. 10, 2026, in Charlotte. Getty Images

At 38, Stafford has endured enough injuries and medical consultations to understand that deciding whether to undergo surgery isn't always as simple as listening to one doctor.

"There's a lot of really smart people out there that have opinions on how things should go," Stafford said. "But in the end, you've got to find people who you trust, go with those people and make a decision."

Stafford acknowledged that some of his own medical decisions were straightforward. Others weren't.

"Luckily, a lot of the stuff I've had has been pretty cut and dry. Either you can or you can't," he said. "But sometimes there are those ones that can go either way."

Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) and Puka Nacua (12) look on against the Philadelphia Eagles on Oct. 4, 2026, at Lincoln Financial Field. Getty Images

That's the cruel reality of professional football. Teams need their stars on Sundays, but players are the ones who must live with the consequences long after the stadium lights go dark.

"We're human beings, too, trying to get our bodies back to do what we love to do," Stafford said.

Stafford said he's remained in contact with Nacua throughout the ordeal, offering encouragement as his teammate begins the long road back.

"He's been a great teammate of mine, and I just want him to feel good again," Stafford said.

#2687. Oregon Ducks set for primetime kickoff vs. Washington Huskies

Senior Day at Autzen Stadium will take place under the bright lights. The Oregon Ducks will host the Washington Huskies for a primetime rivalry matchup, looking to punch their ticket to the Big Ten Championship Game.

The Ducks will take on the Huskies at 4:30 p.m. PST, with the game set to broadcast live on NBC. It's just the third kickoff at Autzen Stadium this season later than 12:30 p.m., but the stakes for the rivalry call for a night game and a rowdy atmosphere.

Washington helped Oregon out on Saturday, knocking off Indiana in Seattle to clear a path for the Ducks to reach the conference title game. While there are some scenarios to keep in mind heading into rivalry weekend, a win over the Huskies will likely push the Ducks to Indianapolis to compete for the conference crown and an automatic bid to the College Football Playoff.

Oregon has won the past two matchups against Washington, including the most recent game in Eugene. Dylan Raiola has been sharp in recent weeks under center, and Oregon's big-play potential on offense could expose part of the Huskies' defense.

However, Washington has strung together a few wins to finish the regular season strong, and the upset against the Hoosiers has given the Huskies plenty of momentum rolling into Eugene. Washington isn't in the running to win the Big Ten, but it could play spoiler to Oregon's playoff hopes. In a rivalry, throw out the records.

Dan Lanning has struggled with the Huskies in his time at Oregon, going 2-3 against the Ducks' northern rival, but the Ducks will be favored at home to get the win and continue their late-season surge.

#2686. AFC North Preview, Week 11: Bengals look to keep separating from the pack

Matchup: @ Philadelphia Eagles, 1:00pm EST

The Steelers came out flat last week despite coming off their bye week. In a primetime spot with the chance to take a first-place lead in the division, the Steelers punted on four of their first five drives. They didn't score a touchdown until the fourth quarter, but it meant little as they were trailing by 28 points. Pittsburgh still has six wins on the season, though, and is set up well to earn a seventh victory in Week 11.

A matchup with the Eagles is much less imposing now than it was several weeks ago, as Philadelphia has been riddled by injuries and traded away several core players. They have lost seven straight games and the last four have come by eight or more points. To avoid a trap game on the road, the Steelers need to avoid turning the ball over and giving the Eagles' offense — which ranks bottom-10 in both the pass and run — any short fields.

The Eagles have vulnerable defending the run this season, allowing 126.1 rushing yards per game. That affords the Steelers an opportunity to get their rushing attack back on track after Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for 41 yards on 12 carries last week. Pittsburgh's passing game continues to be inconsistent as well with D.K. Metcalf struggling as the lead No. 1 wideout. Any potential big play that Aaron Rodgers can connect on through the air will be a bonus.

Following a fifth-straight loss this past Monday to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers, the Ravens' season is officially on life support heading into Week 11. The Ravens were unable to capitalize on turnover opportunities, struggled to defend the run, and committed two costly turnovers of their own. They're now two games under .500 and, in order to keep any semi-possible playoff chances alive, they can't afford to lose any of their next few games.

This week's matchup against the Panthers profiles as perhaps their most favorable contest remaining on the schedule. There are a couple particular areas where the Ravens match up well and need to take advantage. On offense, it's their wide receivers versus Carolina's cornerbacks. The Panthers have been without their starting cornerbacks for several weeks now. They've managed to hold up and rank Top 10 in passing yards allowed, but Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja'Kobi Lane will still have opportunities to win their individual matchups and get open consistently. Given the team's struggles run blocking lately, the Ravens may be better off leaning on Jacoby Brissett's arm and spreading out the defense.

Defensively, the Ravens need to tighten up their coverage over the middle of the field. Bryce Young's biggest strength throwing the ball is targeting that area and the Panthers have been effective doing so this year. They have several tall, athletic pass-catchers that have to be accounted for. It will help if the Ravens can create some pressure and convert sacks. The Panthers' offensive line, particularly their tackles on both sides, has been a weak point. This is a prime spot for Trey Hendrickson to get back in the sack column and for Mike Green to continue his strong run of play recently.

Matchup: @ Washington Commanders, 8:20pm EST

The Bengals continued rolling last week with another convincing divisional win, defeating the Steelers handedly by 20 points (38-18). Led by another MVP-caliber performance from Joe Burrow and signature showing from Ja'Marr Chase, the Bengals led from start to finish — using a 21-point second quarter to quickly pull away. They will hit the road in Week 11 for a second straight primetime outing, this time against the Commanders.

On paper, the Bengals should continue to find success throwing the ball in this game. The Commanders allowed the second-most passing yards per game at over 244 and have a vulnerable secondary. They are much better against the run, but running the ball has not mattered much at all for the Bengals this season. Burrow has been unstoppable airing the ball out to Chase and Tee Higgins, which they will likely continue to lean on here.

The Commanders have been one of the league's most turnover-adverse offenses this season, although Jayden Daniels did throw two fourth-quarter interceptions last week. If the Bengals can force a takeaway or two, it will only strengthen their chances of winning by giving their offense shorter fields. The Bengals match up well defensively with the Commanders but should not let their guard down. Washington has shown an ability to hang around in games and put together late scoring drives.

#2684. Nets say they’re heading in ‘right direction’ after team meeting earlier in week

Danny Wolf rightly stated that the Nets are not looking to accept any moral victories, but they clearly needed a starting point after a debacle of a performance in their previous game earlier in the week against the Bulls.

Friday's tight loss to the Magic at Barclays Center was "a step in the right direction," said veteran forward Julius Randle, the team's most vocal critic during and after the blowout loss to Chicago.

"We competed our tails off, we played really hard and were way more connected as a group on both ends of the floor," said Randle, who had called out the Nets for showing "no pride" during the previous game. "The game is won within the margins, just little things, little possessions. … If we do the little things a bit better, we'll start winning some games and putting some little streaks together."

Moritz Wagner (left) and Noah Clowney high-five during the Nets' loss to the Magic on Nov. 20, 2026 at Barclays Center. NBAE via Getty Images

The three-time All-Star committed a costly turnover in the closing minutes, adding, "I gotta be better, so put that on me." Randle also missed a potential game-winning 3-pointer as time expired in a 113-111 defeat.

"It was a step in the right direction," the former Knick said. "Obviously we want to be on the winning side of things, but it felt like overall just a more connected group out there, talking, communicating. I guess the biggest thing is us as men being able to communicate and hold each other accountable. The coaches are gonna do a great job of holding us accountable, but we have to do it among ourselves too."

The rebuilding Nets (3-12) held a frank team meeting following the 30-point loss to the Bulls, and head coach Jordi Fernández made a key lineup change against Orlando, replacing 2025 lottery pick Egor Dëmin in the starting lineup with Wolf, who netted 20 points.

"You felt the fans, like, they're proud of the group when we play like this, and when we play like the other night [vs. Chicago], we get booed and we deserve it," Fernández said. "[Friday night] we play hard, with purpose, and I think that everybody's proud of that.

"But we've got to continue to do that. At the end of the day, they won the game, and we gotta move on to the next one [Monday at Minnesota]. But if we play like this, we're gonna see a lot of wins. This competitive brand of basketball is how you develop, and obviously we're gonna get what we all want, and that is to win games."

Brooklyn allowed Orlando to connect on 10 of its 19 3-pointers while grabbing a 38-25 advantage in the first quarter, but the Nets came back to take a late lead before falling short.

Julius Randle reacts during the Nets' home loss to the Magic on Nov. 20, 2026 in an NBA Cup game. AP Photo/Frank Franklin II

Dëmin's inconsistencies also continued; he finished with six points on 1-for-6 shooting in 20 minutes in his first appearance of the season off the bench.

"Just keep your head up and keep working, man, stay in the moment, stay present," Randle replied when asked what advice he would give Dëmin, the No. 8 overall pick in 2025. "You can't really worry about whether your shot is falling or not, you just gotta figure out how you can impact winning.

"I know he is hard on [himself], but he's gonna be fine. He's gonna be great. He just has to keep his head up and not let any doubt or negativity creep in. Just look straight ahead and keep working. Obviously, me being a vet, I'll help him with that."

Starting point guard Nolan Traore left Friday's game in the third quarter with a right hamstring injury, meaning Fernández might need to make another lineup change against the Timberwolves.

#2682. Ravens Discussion: Predictions for Week 11 matchup vs. Panthers

The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for this contest.

At this point, it's difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven't had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn't moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No.

X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he's been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations.

I'm not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn't fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter's defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn't seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can't stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win.

X-Factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett's debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren't flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don't think the Jacoby-to-Ja'Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane's skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season.

The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens' recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina's offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week.

X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina's struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher.

The Ravens' playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina's weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers' offensive tackles.

X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young's biggest strength. Smith's coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let's see in this game.

It's hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday.

X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike.

#2680. Wales boss Wilkinson rules out Fishlock return

Rhian Wilkinson says she has not considered asking Jess Fishlock to come out of retirement even though the Wales legend will be on camp for the Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway.

Fishlock ended her playing career earlier this month after her Seattle Reign side lost to Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-offs.

The 39-year-old played on for one final season at Reign having retired from international football in October 2025.

Fishlock will be part of Wales' coaching staff for for next month's two-legged tie against the Norwegians, who come to the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Despite some speculation over whether Fishlock could play some part on the pitch, Wilkinson said: "I think you get retirement right when you know there's still something in you to give."

The Wales boss added: "It takes years to recognise that you got it right, because you're sort of [thinking] 'oh should I've kept playing', but when you get it wrong injuries and someone else makes the decision that you're finished, that's a tough way to to end your career.

"I think Jess has qualified [for Euro 2025], made history with Wales, done such a great job as well as building the game over in the US and equally so much in Wales.

"[But] she's retired. Jess is here to further her technical and tactical awareness, but also for her experiences and that kind of confidence that she brings to the environment."

While there will be no Fishlock, Wales will welcome back a number of experienced players from injury for the Norway games.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway will likely not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

That comes as the team is without Jayson Tatum, Mitchell Robinson, and Derrick White; Tatum is out to rest on the first night of a back-to-back, while Robinson is out with illness. White is out with a shoulder contusion that Mazzulla said he doesn't expect will be a long-term concern.

Mazzulla said he enjoys nights like Saturday, when the team will be shorthanded, and other guys will see more opportunities.

"Who's in, who's out — the standard and expectation stays the same," Mazzulla said. "You gotta be ready to play. Games like this, I enjoy because it validates the locker room and the roster, and guys work hard, put themselves in position to impact winning, and that's what we expect tonight."

Brad Stevens weighed in on the logjam at the wing position at shootaround on Saturday.

"I said at the start of the year, the biggest challenge for the coaching staff is the wing differentiation," Stevens said. "That's been the hardest part, and I think they've managed it beautifully, because nobody has really differentiated themselves, and they're all good players. And so that's just kind of the hard part about having depth, which in this league you need now. It's really important, but it also comes with the challenges of — not everybody's going to get exactly what they want on every given night. Is it easier to have seven or eight guys that you know are going to play every night? Yeah, until two of them get hurt, then you're in trouble, right? And so that's part of the challenge in this day and age with how the league is going and how hard it is to play the full 82, and certainly game to game with what's required on both ends."

Mazzulla said he didn't give players a heads-up on who will start or who will get more opportunities in the wake of the absences.

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2677. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The big prize of this free agent class is ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. We've seen and will continue to see predictions that he's going to land a deal of around 8-10 years and topping $400 million. The knee-jerk reaction to such prognostications in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

Let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the signing team is getting a surefire ace for several years.

Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

Since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the big-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

Skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. If he signs an eight-year deal, it'll run through his age-37 season.

For those so worried about the long-term finances of the team owner who ends up signing Skubal, are you sure you're really worried that he won't be productive through five, six, seven or even all eight years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

Gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

Justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

David Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

Corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

Max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

We can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:

Are you sure a 10-year, $400 million deal for this guy would be a "risk?"

I think we could argue that it would be a bargain.

#2676. Knicks' Mikal Bridges drills buzzer-beating 3-pointer to defeat Trail Blazers

The New York Knicks are rounding into form, and maybe Saturday night is what Mikal Bridges needed to get back on track, too.

The 30-year-old wing, who came into a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers shooting just north of 40% from the field and a smidge above 30% from deep, drilled a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to deliver New York a 97-96 victory in Madison Square Garden.

Bridges finished with 12 points on 5-of-8 shooting. He connected on two of his three attempts from long range. The last one extended the Knicks' win streak to four games.

Following a pair of Deni Avdija free throws that put the Trail Blazers (10-6) up 96-94, New York (10-6) took a timeout. With 3.2 seconds remaining, Josh Hart inbounded the ball to Bridges.

He caught the pass to the right of the top of the arc, used a quick fake to get an overzealous Toumani Camara to bite, took one more dribble and launched.

The ball rattled in, the buzzer sounded and Mike Breen exclaimed, "BANG! BANG!"

Bridges was swarmed by his Knicks teammates, eventually wearing a smile as MSG reveled in utter pandemonium.

He came to the rescue on a night when New York squandered a 26-point lead. The Knicks shot 13 of 27 from 3-point land in the first half but scored only 31 points over the final two quarters.

Bridges admitted afterward that Portland played "harder" than New York in the second half.

But he also noted in that on-court postgame interview: "It's 48 minutes. We just kept persevering through the time and ended up winning the game."

After trailing 94-84 with less than five minutes to go, the Trail Blazers went on a 12-0 run, which culminated in the aforementioned Avdija makes at the charity stripe. Additionally, that stretch featured a game-tying 3-pointer from Damian Lillard.

Avdija was sent to the line because of a head-scratching foul by Knicks center Andre Drummond, who switched and committed the personal on the floor well beyond the arc.

Avdija had 20 points. Center Donovan Clingan spearheaded Portland's effort with 22 points and 13 rebounds. Lillard put up just 15 points and shot a meager 1 of 9 from outside.

New York was paced by Jalen Brunson's 30 points. Fellow guard Landry Shamet poured in 20 points.

Bridges, though, was the hero, sinking a redemptive shot 16 games into what's been a trying season for the ninth-year pro.

#2675. J.J. McCarthy showing improved touch on passes since joining Giants

One of the knocks on J.J. McCarthy during his relatively brief time with the Vikings was his inability to throw anything other than a fastball.

His touch on intermediate and shorter throws was questioned, as was his accuracy when it came to layering the ball over a defender to reach the intended target.

In McCarthy's seven weeks with the Giants, those are not appropriate critiques.

His big-time throw rate and average depth of target rate are in the upper tier among starting quarterbacks.

In the Week 10 loss to the Commanders, McCarthy expertly floated the ball over cornerback Trey Amos and into the hands of rookie Malachi Fields for a 25-yard completion.

Before he ever arrived in a trade to the Giants, McCarthy last offseason worked on his touch down the field with his quarterback coach, John Beck.

The intention of those drills in Orange County, Calif., was to add some finesse to his passes rather than attempt high-velocity throws when a lighter touch was needed.

"I feel like growing up in Chicago, obviously the Windy City, there's a lot of times where you'd cut it through that wind, and that was my way of doing it as a younger kid,'' McCarthy said. "And then also, in the offseason, you can't go outside. So, we were confined to spaces that only have 15-20-foot ceilings. So, it was something that I really had to grow in and develop in.''

This was not an easy adjustment for McCarthy.

J.J. McCarthy talks with reporters earlier this week at the Giants' practice facility. Robert Sabo for New York Post

"To really make it concrete and have that feel consistently, it was pretty hard,'' he said. "It's even harder when you've got guys steamrolling, trying to break you and different guys that are running at different speeds, and there's so many factors that go into that touch.''

The Giants cut Charlie Jones and signed Xavier Gipson off the Eagles practice squad because "we feel like we need a spark'' on kickoff and punt returns, according to special teams coordinator Chris Horton.

This is Gipson's third appearance on the Giants roster — he was on and off the team twice in 2025 — and he has averaged 25.9 yards on 51 career kickoff returns and 9.1 yards on 74 punt returns. The risk here is that Gipson has 12 fumbles in 41 games, losing five of them.

"I truly believe that no player is the same player until he shows you he's the same player,'' Horton said. "So, it's our job to go out there and allow him to grow from those things that might have set him back. But I also know that this guy, when that ball has not been on the ground, he's made teams pay.''

This will be the Jaguars debut for two starting defensive players acquired at the trade deadline: safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis.

This is the second time the Giants will face Davis this season. He had three tackles (two for loss), one sack and one quarterback hit for the Eagles on Nov. 8 in their 19-11 loss in Philadelphia.

"What I really hope to see is for them to obviously know what they're doing and have that be priority No. 1 — alignment, assignment, communication — from that standpoint,'' Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said. "And then just go cut it loose, let it rip, go be you. Go be who got you here. The type of player you are. You don't need to do anything special because it's your first game as a Jaguar. We just need you to be you, and that's probably going to be good enough."

#2674. Dwight Howard makes shocking NBA trade admission that would have sent Stephen Curry to Magic

Dwight Howard makes shocking NBA trade admission that would have sent Stephen Curry to Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

When the Golden State Warriors drafted Stephen Curry in the 2009 NBA Draft, there was skepticism around an immediate impact on the league from the point guard. And Dwight Howard was no different.

The former Orlando Magic star turned down a trade for Curry back in 2011 when the front office proposed one. But more than a decade after the missed opportunity, Howard is regretting his past decision.

The former NBA center recently revisited the decision during an appearance on "The AM Hoops Show," where he recalled Orlando's interest in Curry and his own preference for Monta Ellis at the time.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"The Magic wanted to get Steph, and I said no," Howard recalled. "I said no because I didn't know. I didn't know Wardell Steph Curry was gonna be one of the greatest shooters in the world."

Howard's preference for Ellis was understandable at the time. Ellis was an established scorer in Golden State, while Curry was dealing with recurring ankle injuries that limited his availability. Curry appeared in just 26 games during the 2011-12 season, adding uncertainty to his long-term outlook.

The Warriors eventually traded Ellis to Milwaukee in March 2012, keeping Curry as part of their plans. Curry underwent another ankle procedure that April before signing a four-year extension with Golden State that offseason.

The decision paid off. Curry averaged 22.9 points per game in 2012-13 and helped the Warriors reach the playoffs. He eventually became a two-time MVP and led Golden State to four NBA championships.

Howard's time in Orlando was also nearing its end. After requesting a trade, the eight-time All-Star eventually left the Magic for the Los Angeles Lakers in August 2012, ending an eight-season run with the franchise.
