#2649. MLB rumors: Rangers in mix for Sato, Dodgers seek infield help, Korean slugger could join free agent class

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with only one significant transaction: Evan Phillips signed with the Braves. Phillips, our 34th-ranked free agent, received a three-year deal worth $35 million. He'll replace Raisel Iglesias in Atlanta's bullpen and pair with Robert Suarez at the end of the game. The Braves could still re-sign Iglesias too, I suppose.

Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors -- A LOT of rumors -- and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

The Rangers are among the teams with interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports The Athletic. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers, though he does not stand out defensively, and could land at first base or in the corner outfield in MLB. Texas could stand to upgrade at first base and could always slot Sato in at DH as well.

We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available and the best free agent position player. The reigning Triple Crown winner in Japan hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs in 2026. Sato, 28 in March, has some similarities to Munetaka Murakami as a lefty with big power and swing-and-miss concerns, though Sato is a much more aggressive hitter and won't walk as much as Murakami.

With Miguel Rojas retired, the Dodgers are looking to add a right-handed hitting infielder, according to The Athletic. Mookie Betts and Max Muncy are entrenched on the left side of the infield. Tommy Edman, a switch-hitter, is penciled in at second base, with fellow switch-hitter Alex Freeland next in line as depth. Freeland has not hit much in his limited MLB time, however.

This is not a great free agent class overall, but it does feature several utility infielders who hit right-handed. Among them are Mauricio Dubón, Ha-Seong Kim, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, and Edmundo Sosa. Glovemen Oswald Peraza (Angels) and Jared Triolo (Pirates) are potential trade targets. Rojas was a very productive role player for Los Angeles. He won't be so easy to replace.

The Padres are receiving calls about catchers Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Top prospect Ethan Salas was called up in September and became the youngest catcher to appear in the postseason in Game 2 of the Wild Card Series. Salas is the future behind the plate, making Campusano or Fermin (or perhaps both) expendable.

Campusano and Fermin are very different players. Campusano is a bat-first catcher who might be worth keeping given his age (28) and the fact that the Padres could slot him at DH. That said, those same qualities make him appealing to other teams. Fermin, 31, is a terrific defender who hasn't hit much the last few years. The Padres need pitching and could deal a catcher or two for an arm or two.

Samsung Lions outfielder Ja-Wook Koo has hired a new agent and is looking to make the jump to MLB, reports MLB.com. Koo, a 10-time All-Star and this year's Korean Series MVP, has been among the best hitters in the Korea Baseball Organization the last few years. The 33-year-old hit .371/.458/.581 with 15 homers and nearly as many walks (66) as strikeouts (71) in 2026.

Koo's age and the fact he's a left-handed hitter in a market inundated with left-handed hitting outfielders will work against him in free agency. He has a great track record in Korea, though, including a history of high contact rates, which could make him a cheaper and more appealing target than MLB free agents like Michael Conforto, Trent Grisham, Cedric Mullins, and Daulton Varsho.

#2647. FIFA under pressure to take action over Iran's ban on men watching women's football matches

Human rights campaigners have called on FIFA to take action after an order was issued to ban men from attending women's football matches in Iran.

Last month, a letter from the Iran Football League Organization circulated to its member clubs, which was widely reported on in the Middle East and has been verified by The Athletic, stated that "the presence of men at stadiums hosting women's football matches is prohibited".

Mohammad Reza Keshavari-Fard, the secretary of the league who signed the letter, added that a game's host club "shall be held liable for all resulting consequences" should the order be breached.

While women have been permitted restricted access to attend certain international qualifiers and high-profile men's league fixtures in Iran since December 2023 following sustained pressure from human rights campaigners and FIFA, the presence of men at women's matches in Iran has been a complex issue in recent years.

Men have technically not been permitted to attend women's football matches, though exceptions have been made for coaching staff, officials, family members, media members and other matchday and technical staff, eventually extending to spectators.

The new order overrides these exceptions and, in doing so, appears to breach the rules of FIFA, world football's governing body. FIFA's Statutes state that discrimination based on gender — including exclusion or interference with access to stadiums — is "strictly prohibited and punishable by suspension or expulsion". In 2017, FIFA adopted a Human Rights policy pledging to "apply effective leverage" to strengthen "human rights in or through football".

Human Rights Watch, Amnesty International and the Sport & Rights Alliance have now all called on FIFA to address the issues and enforce its statutes. Each organisation referenced the long-running struggle for Iranian women to attend men's football games in the country. "That struggle is not over, and now Iran seems to be finding new ways to discriminate against women in football by barring male journalists, referees and coaches from attending women's matches," Andrea Florence, executive director of the Sport & Rights Alliance, said in a statement to The Athletic.

When contacted by The Athletic, FIFA highlighted its non-discrimination statute and its president Gianni Infantino's public support for the presence of women at men's football games in Iran.

The directive from the league came ahead of the first-ever women's derby between Tehran rivals Esteghlal and Persepolis, Iran's two most successful men's clubs.

That match was delayed by five days from Friday, October 23 until Wednesday, October 28 and moved to a smaller stadium on the outskirts of Tehran. Friday is a weekly rest day in Iran, with Wednesday a working day. Persepolis won the historic meeting 2-1.

A report in Iran International, which one source has confirmed to The Athletic, details how ticket sales were suspended twice in the days ahead of the match. Female fans were allowed to attend, but no males were present at the match.

Mooud Bonyadifard, a high-profile male Iranian referee who has been FIFA-listed since 2013, had initially been appointed to be the video assistant referee (VAR) for the derby, but was not part of the officiating team due to the new directive.

Zahra Behrouz Azar, Iran's vice president for women and family affairs, attended the women's Tehran derby, and called for greater access for Iranians to attend future events.

"Many Iranians were eager to witness up close today, in this historic derby, the brilliance and standout performances of Iran's women's footballers, who have shone time and again on the international stage," Behrouz Azar posted.

"This opportunity was not available to all supporters. We are working to make it possible for all fans to attend and watch these moments."

In Iran, separation between men and women attending the same football matches has been a long-running issue.

In December 2023, women were allowed into a men's derby between Persepolis and Esteghlal in Iran's capital.

Female fans had been banned from attending men's matches across the country since 1981, two years after the nation's Islamic Revolution. For more than four decades, female protestors and campaigners tried to circumvent the ban — often by dressing up as men. The state responded with arrests, beatings and forced exiles.

Restrictions on women's attendance at these games remain in place; there are limited ticket numbers, women are obliged to sit in a separate section from men in the stands, and several stadiums still do not allow their presence at such matches.

Iran's ban was never written into law but became a practice enforced by the country's 'morality police', which enforces Sharia.

However, there are concerns from some inside and outside of Iran that the sport access granted to women in the country may be under threat. Recent reports in Iran have highlighted how women are no longer be permitted to use the outdoor running track in the capital's Keshvari Stadium, as of October 23, following a decision by the facility's management. The decision to ban men from women's football was announced shortly after.

"FIFA is violating its own human rights rules by letting Iran's football federation (FFIRI) get away with blatant discrimination," Minky Worden, director of global initiatives at Human Rights Watch, told The Athletic.

"The courageous women footballers in Iran can no longer have their fathers, brothers and male coaches watch them play. FIFA's own statutes say gender discrimination in stadium access is 'strictly prohibited and punishable by suspension or expulsion'.

"In 2017, FIFA also pledged to 'apply effective leverage' on human rights. It should use that leverage now instead of opening another fake conversation."

Worden added: "For more than four decades, FIFA self-servingly refused to punish Iran's ban on women in stadiums — constantly pursuing useless dialogue with the abusive Iranian government officials who run the FFIRI, the same officials who were ruthlessly harassing, beating and arresting women and girls who were trying to assert their right to go to football matches."

Florence, of the Sport & Rights Alliance, also called on FIFA to "urgently use its leverage to address this discrimination", telling The Athletic: "In the past, FIFA has successfully used its influence to allow women fans into stadiums in Iran – at one point with its own staff standing at the gates.

Amnesty International researcher Mansoureh Mills has said the latest development of men not being allowed to attend women's football shows "the Iranian authorities now appear to be doubling down on discrimination.

"Iran must end discriminatory restrictions on access to football and respect women's and girls' equal participation in sport and public life."

Following the partial return of women to men's football matches in 2023, Infantino linked the development to FIFA's communication with the Iranian federation. In a social media post, he said: "Thanks to the ongoing dialogue between FIFA and the FFIRI, progress is being made."

FIFA sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to allow them to do so candidly, indicate that the governing body would continue to pursue an approach of dialogue with the FFIRI, as they believe this is the most effective approach for progress.

Between 2018 and 2021, Iran was the only nation to ban the presence of women at men's football games. That was the period between Saudi Arabia lifting its own long-standing ban, and the return of Taliban rule in Afghanistan, which diminished the rights and freedoms of women across that country. Women can no longer attend football matches in Afghanistan, where they are banned from participating in sport.

In November 2025, FIFA president Infantino acknowledged the "encouraging development" of the presence of female fans at a Hazfi Cup match between Nassaji Mazandaran and Shahid Ghandi Yazd in Mashhad, Iran's second-largest city. Open Stadiums said only limited numbers of women were allowed into that game, played between two lower-league clubs.

The Athletic has approached the FFIRI for comment.

This article originally appeared in The Athletic.

The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be an RB column, a WR column and this combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

1. Joe Burrow (at WAS) - 25.0 proj. points

Burrow is playing like the MVP. He's scored 24.6+ fantasy points in seven straight games, depending on the scoring system. His +0.26 EPA per dropback is fourth, and he's doing it on the highest neutral pass rate (67%) by a wide margin. He's at his mental and physical peak.

The Commanders defense has allowed the sixth-most half PPR points per game to QBs (20.8), and opposing offenses pass 59% of the time in neutral situations against Washington (third). Sign me up. The Bengals roll in as 6.5-point road favorites, carrying a 30.5-point implied team total (third).

2. Josh Allen (vs. MIA) - 23.4 proj. points

Another year of Allen averaging 26.3 fantasy points per game, which somehow is QB2 behind Joe Burrow. The only real change this year is the presence of a real downfield threat in DJ Moore, who scored a post TD and hit on a couple of crossing routes last game now that he's actually healthy.

The Dolphins just placed three key DTs on injured reserve and are quite inexperienced in the back. Allen's history against the Dolphins is exquisite. He's been a top-10 fantasy QB in 9 of 10 outings against them since 2022, with five top-5 games. Buffalo enters as 16.5-point home favorites with a 31.0-point implied team total (second).

3. Dak Prescott (vs. TEN) - 22.2 proj. points

Prescott is coming off his best performance of the year, hanging 343 passing yards and five touchdowns on the 49ers in Week 10. That's what will happen whenever he's pushed because the defense is failing, as usual. Prescott is currently the QB5 in fantasy, while sitting eighth in EPA per dropback. He's having a great season again.

The Titans aren't. They've allowed the most passing yards per game (282) and are on the worst three-game stretch of their team's history based on total yards allowed. It's hovering around 1,500 yards. Yikes. They won't have superstar DT Jeffery Simmons, nor S Amani Hooker moving forward. Dallas enters as 8.5-point home favorites with the top implied team total of the week at 31.5 points (first).

4. Caleb Williams (vs. NO) - 20.9 proj. points

Fresh off the bye, Williams is hoping to hit his stride after an injury and difficult schedule slowed him down to open the year. He's the QB12 on a per-game basis (19.8), including his rain/hamstring clunker against the Vikings. He's been the QB4 in passing yards since then but hasn't run as often (9.5 YPG). That hopefully will change after the break.

Week 11 brings a home date against a Saints defense that allows the 22nd-most half PPR points to opposing QBs (17.5 per game). New Orleans can rush the passer fairly well, but it's been terrible at tackling and can be run on at will. The Bears could lean on that here, but there's nothing about the LB and DB rooms to be fearful of. New Orleans is 11th in pass YPG and sixth in rush YPG. The Bears head into Sunday as 11.5-point home favorites with a stout 30-point implied team total (fourth).

5. Jayden Daniels (vs. CIN) - 21.1 proj. points

Daniels is not rushing nearly as often the last month (19.3 YPG) as he typically does, which has kept him in check in fantasy as the QB11. They aren't calling designed QB runs, so we're at the mercy of unstable scrambling production. That can return at any point, however, and this is a matchup that should incentivize just that. The Bengals are weakest at LB by far and there are more scrambles while chasing points. Washington is listed as 6.5-point home underdogs carrying a 24-point implied team total (11th). This is a spot to chase the ceiling. Cincy has allowed the second-most rushing yards per game to QBs versus their opponents' seasonal average.

6. Patrick Mahomes (vs. ARI) - 20.3 proj. points

Mahomes exploded for 348 yards and five passing touchdowns against Atlanta in Week 10, bringing his season-long baseline up to QB6 (20.8 PPG). He has delivered +0.15 EPA per dropback (QB9) across his nine starts while chipping in 11.1 rushing yards per game (28th). I can make the case that the return of Rashee Rice and the addition of Josh Downs have the pass game in the best spot of the year right now.

Plus, the Cardinals defense can't stop anyone, allowing the third-most fantasy points to QBs this season. Matthew Stafford turned in three scores despite missing his top receivers last week, and Dak Prescott (QB11), Bo Nix (QB3) and Jared Goff (QB4) have all lit it up since September. It's not a surprise to see the Chiefs projected for 28.5 points (sixth). They may not have Kenneth Walker III (groin) either, which could mean additional throwing production on the margins.

7. C.J. Stroud (vs. IND) - 21 proj. points

Stroud is the QB4 this season, averaging 274 passing YPG (QB3) with 2.1 TDs (QB6). The Texans have much better WR depth now than before, while still struggling to run the ball with any consistency. Houston is suddenly fifth in neutral pass rate (57%), and the Colts are missing all of their best defenders in CB1 Sauce Gardner, CB2 Charvarius Ward and DT1 DeForest Buckner. Recent fantasy QB1s Dak Prescott (336 yards) and Trevor Lawrence (three scores) have come through against them. Houston enters Thursday night as 12.5-point home favorites sporting a strong 28.5-point implied team total (fifth).

8. Trevor Lawrence (at NYG) - 18.8 proj. points

Lawrence has been in a groove as fantasy's QB8 (20.7 PPG), generating +0.29 EPA per dropback (QB3) with 21 passing touchdowns across nine starts. The only issue at times is not having a ton of volume due to game script, as the Jaguars easily lead the NFL in point differential. They're actually 31st all time in that metric through nine games.

This matchup is expected to be a bit closer, partially because the Giants defense has outkicked expectations. They've still allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to QBs, despite getting breakouts from rookie LB Arvell Reese and CB1 Deonte Banks. They're well coached with solid safety play. Where they've been lit up is against the scramble, as both Tyler Shough and Jayden Daniels have run like crazy. That's unlikely for Lawrence, so a more mediocre output wouldn't be too surprising. Jacksonville travels as 6-point road favorites with an implied team total of 26.25 points (seventh).

Bo Nix has more games below 10.0 fantasy points (three) than he does above 20.0 (two) so far. It's largely the same issues as in previous seasons, but to his credit, things historically have looked way better in the second half of seasons. I haven't noticed that he's a worse athlete coming off the dislocated ankle. It's more of just decision-making inside the pocket, but hopefully Sean Payton got into his head during this bye week. Hopefully Jaylen Waddle was listening, too!

To be fair, Nix has had the third-hardest schedule to date and the easiest schedule moving forward. This week kicks that off. The Raiders have been horrific on defense in both phases. They've allowed the second-most fantasy points to QBs and the second-most rushing yards to all positions. That's difficult to do! Nix has been the QB17, QB23, QB8 and QB8 against the Raiders historically, but this defense's current six-game streak of allowing a top-13 fantasy QB is more important. Denver is set up well as 10-point home favorites with a 25.25-point team total (eighth).

10. Jared Goff (vs. TB) - 17.9 proj. points

Goff's weird schedule is behind him after facing the Vikings, traveling outside to Miami and then ending up in Germany. Back in Detroit, Goff should normalize. He was the QB4 from Weeks 1-7 before all that and still is the QB6 in EPA per dropback and QB5 in passing yards per game.

This is still not an easy matchup, though. The Buccaneers bring the heat, something that has historically bothered Goff. Tampa Bay has an awesome CB duo and more depth along the defensive line, while still being coached by a Super Bowl winner. The Bucs are the fourth-best fantasy QB defense, despite everyone knowing this is a relative pass funnel (32nd in rush YPG). Caleb Williams squeaked by as the QB9 in Week 9, but they haven't allowed a top-10 since Week 2 otherwise. The Lions return home as 7-point home favorites with a solid 25.25-point implied team total (ninth).

11. Brock Purdy (vs. MIN) - 19.1 proj. points

Purdy is balling. He's the QB2 in EPA per dropback, as usual, but because he's making more plays out of structure and running around, Purdy is suddenly the QB3 in fantasy this year. That's impressive considering the WRs he's had at times, and Keenan Allen being around is a great way to calm down that room.

They'll need to be calm against the blitz-crazy Vikings. Minnesota hasn't just been the best fantasy QB defense — it's been an all-time unit. My site has a schedule-adjusted metric that essentially shows how many fantasy points each defense allows versus their opponents' seasonal average. The Vikings allowed 8.5 fewer points than QBs' averages. That's insane. Next closest is 4.3 points below average. Whew.

For context, if Purdy scores 8.5 fewer points than his 23.2 average, then he'd be the QB25. I don't think it'll be that bad because he has Kyle Shanahan and a better OL than others who have struggled, but Jordan Love (QB23), Josh Allen (QB17) and Jared Goff (QB21) are all fantasy QB1s, yet didn't finish like one in the most recent games against Minnesota. San Francisco enters Sunday night as 3-point home favorites with a 24.25-point implied team total (10th).

12. Cam Ward (at DAL) - 17.4 proj. points

This is the best Ward projection of his entire career. He's playing a bit better of late with the coaching staff meeting him halfway with their scheme. They've upped their no-huddle rate to the top of the league recently, and he's been running a bit more this month (23 rushing YPG) than he typically does. Ward is still too loose with things and has cleared 20.0 fantasy points in only three games this year, but if there's a time to view him as an upside QB2, it's now.

The Cowboys are just that bad. They've taken away play-calling duties from their DC, to summarize their season. They've been fifth-worst against fantasy QBs on the eighth-most passing yards per game (252). They've also allowed the most rushing yards per game (154). Offenses tend to play balanced ball against Dallas, but if Carnell Tate (shoulder) returns, then the Titans should take their chances downfield, too. Tennessee is listed as an 8.5-point road underdog with an implied total of 23 points (13th).

13. Bryce Young (vs. BAL) - 16.7 proj. points

14. Justin Herbert (vs. NYJ) - 16.5 proj. points

15. Tyler Shough (at CHI) - 16.0 proj. points

16. Kirk Cousins (at SF) - 14.8 proj. points

18. J.J. McCarthy (vs. JAX) - 15.3 proj. points

19. Geno Smith (at LAC) - 14.5 proj. points

20. Jacoby Brissett (at CAR) - 15.2 proj. points

21. Aaron Rodgers (at PHI) - 13.5 proj. points

22. Joe Milton III (vs. PIT) - 14.4 proj. points

23. Fernando Mendoza (at DEN) - 11.9 proj. points

24. Kyle McCord (at BUF) - 10.1 proj. points

25. Daniel Jones (at HOU) - 10.7 proj. points

1. Colston Loveland (vs. NO) - 50.5 proj. yards

Loveland is the TE5 on TE3 usage since Week 6, when Caleb Williams returned. In his last 10 games together dating back to late in his rookie season, Loveland is averaging 11.4 half PPR points on 13.2 expected points, making him a fringe elite TE1. The true elites have disappeared with Brock Bowers healthy and the Cardinals projected for 12.5 points, so Loveland has a real case to take over as the short-term TE1 overall.

The Saints defense ranks sixth in half PPR points allowed to TEs at 13.1 per game, and they don't have the LB/S play to worry about. Harold Fannin Jr. had one of the best reps of the season against them in Week 9, and Isaiah Likely hung 99-1 on them over their last month of games. Chicago enters as 11.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 30 points (fourth).

2. Trey McBride (at KC) - 48.5 proj. yards

McBride's fantasy case has taken a hit due to the wild injury "luck" the Cardinals have run into. Last week, the offense couldn't run the ball, nor stop the run on the other side. The Cardinals ended up with 34 plays on offense, one of the lowest of the entire century. McBride still had five receptions and a 30% target share, while competing with Yahoo fantasy analysts for targets. My eyes tell me Carson Beck isn't quite as bad as what last week's box score showed. The INTs weren't his fault, and he didn't seem panicked. His accuracy is definitely worse than Jacoby Brissett's, but McBride is so QB-friendly that I tend to believe he'll survive despite the shocking result last week.

Kansas City sits eighth in half PPR points allowed to TEs (12.8 per game), while opposing offenses face them with a 45% neutral pass rate that ranks 32nd (lowest). There won't be much "neutral" game script here, however. The Cardinals will quickly get the ball out to McBride all game. The Chiefs have awesome CBs to take away all WRs, and they're a bit worse at stopping quick throws over the middle. A 12.5-point team total stares us down deep into our souls.

3. George Kittle (vs. MIN) - 47.5 proj. yards

Kittle enters as the TE6 on TE1 usage over his last four games, averaging 8.3 targets and 13.1 expected half PPR points per contest. He earned a 30% target share across that window and drew at least eight targets in three of those four appearances. There's more target competition now that Keenan Allen is in and Deebo Samuel Sr. is back, but he's been balling by any measure.

Of course, the Vikings are just as awesome. They've allowed the fewest fantasy points to TEs (6.7 per game) and the second-fewest passing yards (191 per game). Offenses tend to keep their TEs in to block more often against this blitz-heavy unit, and they've passed the ball in neutral situations at the second-lowest rate. Nothing about this works in Kittle's favor. This is simply great versus great. This is must-watch TV. San Francisco is listed as 3-point home favorites with an implied total of 24.25 points (10th).

4. T.J. Hockenson (at SF) - 44.5 proj. yards

Adding Kirk Cousins, who is a TE magnet historically, and subtracting Jordan Addison is an ideal run out for Hockenson. He's already the TE9 on TE9 usage this season, too. I'm very open to him finishing as an every-week TE1 down the stretch. A matchup with Fred Warner and the 49ers isn't ideal, but the Vikings haven't trailed too often this season, and they just might here.

5. Isaiah Likely (vs. JAX) - 49.5 proj. yards

Update: Likely (groin) is dealing with a "minor thing" but should be fine per coach John Harbaugh, who can be hard to trust with injuries historically. The added uncertainty only works against him on the margins.

Likely leads all tight ends as the TE1 on TE5 usage across his last four games, averaging 15.0 half PPR points on a 24% target share. He has scored in three of those four contests, peaking with a 9-127-1 line on 11 targets last week with J.J. McCarthy. He's way too important as the clear-cut No. 2 target to not get home whenever the Giants are pushed.

They are 6-point home dogs against the pass-funnel Jaguars this week. They've been stout against fantasy TEs (8.7 half PPR per game), but Likely is more of a slot WR than anything. Offenses facing them have passed at the second-highest rate in neutral situations (59%), and the Giants may be forced into more dropbacks than they want to if their defense can't stop this Jags offense.

6. Brock Bowers (at DEN) - 50.5 proj. yards

Update: Bowers (ankle) appeared to have a high-ankle sprain, then went DNP-limited-limited in practice this week. Nobody has been confident either way on if he plays, but if he does, it'd be a surprise if he's fully himself. Even a somewhat hobbled Bowers is capable of a big game, but there is no floor anymore. The Broncos also have CB1 Patrick Surtain to match up with him when he's out there, and Bowers has only had 46, 27, 38 and 97 yards against the Broncos historically. There are real reasons to dock him in projections this week, yet there probably isn't a better option on your bench either.

7. Travis Kelce (vs. ARI) - 40.5 proj. yards

8. Chig Okonkwo (vs. CIN) - 40.5 proj. yards

9. Sam LaPorta (vs. TB) - 35.5 proj. yards

10. Brenton Strange (at NYG) - 32.5 proj. yards

11. Mark Andrews (at CAR) - 33.5 proj. yards

Andrews' 8-82-0 game last week came out of nowhere. He looked smooth on tape after being pretty clunky throughout the year. There was a report that he's been playing with a broken hand since Week 3. Equally as helpful as not having a broken body part that's very commonly used to catch an object is having dropback-heavy Jacoby Brissett at QB. He's targeted this position throughout his career as a risk-averse PPR scam artist. Keep in mind the Ravens have averaged 29.7 dropbacks per game since 2022, which is easily the fewest.

The matchup is just fine. The Panthers are solid at LB and are healthy along the DL, but they've been just average against the position. The Ravens' 20.5-point team total is also just average.

12. Tyler Warren (at HOU) - 37.5 proj. yards

I watched all of Warren's 2026 targets this week to get a feel for what's going on, and I came away without too much of an opinion either way. There are some moments of straight-line athleticism and plenty of physicality-based wins, but his route-running chops and fluidity are closer to average. The Colts haven't figured out how to get him unlocked beyond 5ish yards from the line of scrimmage, and they are run-heavy in the red zone, so it's hard for Warren to find a ceiling.

In theory, Warren should be a PPR scam while the offense tanks without their top-3 WRs. In practice, it hasn't happened. Warren is the TE13 on TE7 usage this month on a 22% target share. Better days are coming out of desperation for targets, but the offense seems content handing it off to both of their good-looking backs right now.

The Texans won't have LB Azeez Al-Shaair, but the Colts won't have All-Pro LG Quenton Nelson, nor their starting OTs. Daniel Jones is about to get crushed, and Warren might be tasked with chip and releases on Thursday Night Football. It's possible the score gets so lopsided that the target volume is overwhelming, but it's a tough needle to thread with the Colts projected for 16.0 points. Warren has been the TE13, TE23 and TE11 against the Texans to start his career.

13. Mike Gesicki (at WAS) - 24.5 proj. yards

The Commanders have allowed the second-most fantasy points to TEs (16.9) despite having LB Sonny Styles, and the Bengals project for over 30 points while on fire. "Who is scoring the red-zone touchdown?" is a fun game to play while we have six teams on bye. Isaiah Likely just posted 127 yards with a score against them last week after finishing as the TE1 overall in Week 5, too. They aren't totally similar, but there is some overlap.

#2643. Trinity Rodman says third straight NWSL final loss 'hurts way worse' than others

WASHINGTON, DC — The Washington Spirit have now lost three straight NWSL Championship games. According to Trinity Rodman, this one was by far the most painful.

Playing on their home turf, the Spirit fell short in a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current on Saturday, Nov. 21. Even with the backing of a sold-out Audi Field crowd, the Spirit could not overcome a physical, organized Current side.

Kansas City's approach was exemplified by an incident just five minutes in. Rodman received a ball with her back to Current defender Laney Rouse, who clattered into the Spirit star with considerable force.

The 24-year-old went down in agony, grabbing her left shoulder. After several minutes, she returned to the game, but the message had been sent.

Rodman said the tackle "hurt really bad" but the bigger issue in her mind was that the Current were the team delivering it — not the Spirit.

"As a team, you always want to put that first tackle out," she said. "You're taught to make the first hit. So credit to that because I wish I was the one that put her on the ground."

But it was Rouse who put Rodman on the ground, one of 35 total fouls on the night. The Current set out to disrupt the Spirit, who scored six goals in two previous playoff games. They accomplished that task with gusto.

"It felt like we couldn't play more than two minutes without a whistle," Rodman said.

It was bitterly ironic for Rodman, who played through injury in each of the team's previous two title games. After entering Saturday's game healthy, she had to battle through a sore shoulder for the majority of the match.

Rodman still managed to score a late consolation, her first goal in her four title game appearances. But ultimately it was not enough for a Spirit side that will once again have to rue a final when they weren't at their best.

"This one hurts way worse than any of the other ones," Rodman said. "I don't even think you have words in this moment."

#2642. Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

One of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

Kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

Right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

However, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't currently have on their roster.

Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

#2640. Two fighters transported to hospital after UFC Qatar, including former champion’s brother

Following UFC Qatar earlier today (Sat., Nov. 21, 2026) inside ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar, promotion officials confirmed to MMAmania.com that two fighters were transported to a local hospital for precautionary evaluations after sustaining damage in their respective bouts.

Those fighters were Aleksandre Topuria and Nikolas Motta.

Topuria (7-2) was transported for precautionary CT scans of his head and face following his split-decision loss to Santiago Luna in the preliminary-card headliner.

Aleksandre, the older brother of former UFC champion Ilia Topuria, suffered his first Octagon loss and had his five-fight winning streak snapped.

The 30-year-old is now 2-1 inside the promotion, with unanimous decision victories over Colby Thicknesse and Bekzat Almakhan.

Motta (15-7) was also transported for precautionary CT scans of his head and face following his lopsided unanimous decision loss to Dom Mar Fan on the UFC Qatar "Prelims."

Fan battered Motta badly enough that the Brazilian's right eye was nearly swollen shut. A ringside physician was called in to examine Motta and determine whether he could safely continue, but "Iron" ultimately made it to the final bell.

The 33-year-old has now lost two consecutive fights after putting together a two-fight winning streak in 2024. For what it's worth, Motta has also been transported to the hospital following each of his last two appearances.

At the time of publication, the results of Topuria and Motta's scans had not been publicly disclosed.

It is normal for UFC to transport fighters to the hospital for precautionary reasons, especially if the fighters are involved in three-round battles that are full of damage or after suffering nasty knockouts.

#2639. Could Tarik Skubal take a short-term, high-AAV contract? Breaking down pros and cons

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The expectation is left-hander and two-time AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the best free agent available this offseason, will sign a record contract before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Barring a surprise agreement, the owners are almost certain to lock out the players at that time. Skubal is expected to sign before then.

Skubal, 30 later this month, is a Scott Boras client and Boras tends to shatter records, not beat them narrowly. There's a real chance Skubal signs a contract worth more than $400 million in the next two weeks or so. Excluding Shohei Ohtani, who is technically a pitcher but is really a two-way player, here are the largest pitching contracts in history:

Something like, say, eight years at $50 million a year would give Skubal a $400 million contract that obliterates the previous pitcher records for total guarantee and average annual value. Several big-market clubs are said to be pursuing Skubal (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), who is a special free agent as an in-his-prime ace. Conditions are ripe for a record deal.

There is also a chance Skubal goes the Valdez route, or the Bo Bichette/Kyle Tucker route, and signs a short-term contract with a high annual salary. It might only be a small chance, but there is a chance. The Athletic reports the Dodgers prefer such an arrangement with Skubal. ESPN says Skubal has no interest in such a deal, though minds can always be changed.

With that in mind, here are the pros and cons of a high-dollar, short-term contract for Skubal. Keep in mind that such a contract is usually a three- or four-year deal with opt outs, not a straight one- or two-year contract, and Skubal wouldn't necessarily have to use the opt outs to re-enter free agency. He could leverage them into a new contract to stay with his team.

1. Maximize earnings. Plain and simple, a short-term contract would give Skubal a chance to max out his earnings by making free agency available to him again as soon as next offseason. Go out, have a typical Skubal season in 2027, and perhaps market forces push the demand even higher than it is right now. Remember that, along with a salary cap, there could be a salary floor in the future. Small-market contenders like, say, the Guardians or Rays could throw many millions at Skubal to reach the floor in the future.

2. Chance to set more records. This ties back to the last point. Skubal already set a new salary record for an arbitration-eligible player ($32 million in 2026) and he's positioned to set a new standard for pitcher contracts this offseason. Go back into free agency in a year or two, and Skubal (and Boras) could have a chance to break his own pitcher contract record. The record itself won't be a driving factor in that decision (the money will ultimately decide things), but it would be a nice feather in his cap.

3. Freedom to change teams. Sometimes things don't work out. I don't think Juan Soto expected to miss the postseason in the first two years of his record 15-year, $765 million contract with the Mets. It's entirely possible Skubal could find his next situation not to his liking for whatever reason. Maybe the team doesn't contend, maybe he clashes with the coaching staff, maybe he doesn't like the local breakfast taco options. There could be a million different reasons it doesn't work. A short-term, high-dollar deal would give Skubal an escape hatch and allow him to head elsewhere if things go sideways.

1. Injury and performance risk. All things considered, Skubal is a pretty safe bet on a long-term contract, though he is a pitcher, and pitchers get hurt. It's what they do. Skubal has had three elbow surgeries, including Tommy John surgery in 2017 and a minor procedure this May. If he gets hurt again, or his performance slips for whatever reason, then he could wind up costing himself in the big picture because he won't be able to opt out and sign a larger deal. A short-term, high-dollar contract will pay him handsomely. He won't struggle to put bread on the table. But injury/performance risk means Skubal could ultimately leave money on the table.

2. Potential salary cap. It is possible the next CBA will include a salary cap, which could limit Skubal's market and earning potential should he go back out into free agency in a year or two (or three). It's not just the cap itself either. MLB has proposed contract limits as part of the salary cap: five years at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, or six years at 16% of the cap for players who remain with their current team. Even if MLB doesn't get a salary cap and instead the competitive balance tax system remains in place with stiffer penalties, that could cost Skubal in the future. This offseason might be his last chance to sign in a truly free market.

#2637. Texans vs. Colts prediction: Houston looks to bounce back on 'TNF' vs. lowly Indy after rough Week 10 loss

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts.

Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot.

The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline.

Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.

The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.

Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing.

Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL. Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions.

The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games.

The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan, including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up.

Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state.

C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season.

The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner, either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins.

It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence.

This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense.

I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody.

#2636. Blue Jays' Anthony Santander issues statement after sharing anti-Muslim videos: 'This content caused hurt'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander has issued a statement regarding his recent anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted. Santander's statement, which he posted to Instagram and follows a public condemnation of the posts by Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins, reads as follows:

"After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform.

"I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize. I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared, recognizing the responsibility that comes with having a public voice.

"As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs. After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions.

"I would like to affirm my respect for the Muslim community and for the dignity and freedom of people of every faith and background.

"From this experience, I have learned to ensure that none of my communications promote hate or give the impression that I support hatred, discrimination, or violence against anyone."

The club had earlier released a statement on the incident that read:

"Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."

Santander, a Venezuela native, shared social media videos following the recent U.S. midterm elections, including one in which a Christian pastor said, "There is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another suggested that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate representing the state of Michigan.

Atkins told reporters Tuesday that Santander's behavior "did not align" with organizational values and there were no words "to express my level of disappointment."

"I talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant," Atkins said. "We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that."

Santander, 32, joined the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season on a five-year, $92.5 million free-agent contract. He struggled badly across 54 games in 2025 and missed the entire 2026 season with injury.

#2635. NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Celtics win Jaylen Brown trade (for now), Trae Young looks done

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Every now and then, the NBA gives us a week that is essentially built around a single game. A total of 51 games were played in the last week, but come on, the one you remember was Jaylen Brown's long-awaited reunion with Jayson Tatum. The Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers squared off in a battle of the Eastern Conference's two top seeds on Tuesday, and even if the game fell short of our basketball expectations, it provided more than enough beef to sate us. Brown snubbed Tatum before the game. Paul George gave a fan the middle finger. Appropriate animosity has returned to this eternal rivalry.

So... how did we handle that from a winners and losers perspective? Well, Boston is an obvious winner, but Brown escaped loser status. It's winners and losers of the week. Philly won its two other games this week, and Brown led all scorers in Sunday's win with 31 points. He certainly lost on Tuesday. He may yet wind up losing the trade. But we're not docking him a whole week for a single poor performance. So if Brown escaped the loser's section, who made it? And who joins Boston in the winner's circle? Let's look back at the week that was.

Boston's big win over Philadelphia underlined something that's been evident all season: Paul George, at least thus far, has been better as a Celtic than Jaylen Brown has been as a 76er. There are obviously circumstantial reasons for that. George is at his best as a force-multiplier, and he's on a team on which he doesn't need to play an enormous role. Brown is at his best as a floor-raiser, but he's on a team full of floor-raisers. That doesn't mean Philadelphia regrets the trade -- it got them LeBron James! -- but it does suggest that, after months of criticism, the Celtics at least got what they were looking for out of the deal.

Everything the Celtics were good at a year ago, they're still good at. They were one of the NBA's best shooting teams last season, and George both makes more 3s than Brown and takes far more of them. They were great at protecting the basket last season and George's activity as a helper has been a net benefit to their rim-protection.

Yet George's presence has also been the catalyst for improvement in a few other key areas. Boston never generated turnovers defensively last season and they do this year, in part because George is averaging the sixth-most steals and third-most deflections in the NBA. They're getting to the line at a roughly league-average rate, in part because the ball doesn't stick to George as it so often did Brown. It's easier to get defenses in rotation with the ball moving and 3-pointers flying. Tatum has benefited enormously in this respect with a career-best 46% free-throw rate.

Again, the 76ers are perfectly happy with their end of the deal. They traded old for young. They got James on the minimum. They're 11-3. But Boston emerged with the player who has made a bigger difference thus far this season, and it got two first-round draft assets in the process. That doesn't mean the Celtics necessarily win the trade in the long run, but it does suggest, unsurprisingly, that Brad Stevens understood his own team and what it needed better than the rest of us.

Well, they haven't lost in three weeks... so this feels overdue. Let's talk about the much ballyhooed three-guard lineup for a moment. The Spurs couldn't keep bringing Dylan Harper off the bench this season. He's simply too good and too important to their future to risk alienating. They couldn't bench De'Aaron Fox immediately either. Former All-Stars tend to take such decisions as a sign of disrespect, and such a move could have splintered the locker room.

So the Spurs made the somewhat awkward decision to start the three of them together. The season's second game, a loss to the Houston Rockets, showcased exactly why so many feared the fit of the three of them together. Three iffy guard-sized shooters minimized spacing for the sake of redundant ball-handling, and the Harper-Fox-Stephon Castle trio got outscored by 12 points in a four-point defeat. Well, the three guards haven't lost their minutes together in a single game since then. They're +112 in 115 minutes after that point.

Now, there are notable caveats here. Every three-man combination of Spurs that has played at least 100 minutes since then is firmly positive, and the three guards have literally not played a single minute together this season that did not come alongside Victor Wembanyama. It's entirely possible that Wembanyama is so game-breaking that any lineup he's a part of is an almost automatic winner. But that would work in favor of the three guards here. Maybe San Antonio is so much more talented than the field that it can afford to play suboptimal lineups for the sake of maintaining harmony in the locker room.

That may prove more challenging late in a playoff series, but it's easier to convince players to change their roles for, say, Game 5 of the Western Conference Finals than it is in November or December. The Spurs might have to think harder about this in a field that included a healthy Oklahoma City, but with the Thunder compromised, San Antonio is such a large favorite to win the Western Conference that it can afford to try to just out-talent everyone else. So far, it's clearly working.

We are in all-out panic mode over the state of Cleveland's starting lineup. James Harden can't get to the rim anymore. Donovan Mitchell just signed a supermax extension that already feels iffy. Peyton Watson's shooting has fallen off a cliff and he's struggling as a primary point-of-attack defender. The Evan Mobley-Jarrett Allen partnership is getting crushed in its joint minutes. The starters have played 99 minutes together and lost those minutes by 24 points. No five-man unit that has played that many minutes has been outscored by more. Malaise doesn't do this core justice. Clearly, something here has to change.

Fortunately, there appear to be some internal solutions here. After FAA issues forced the Cavaliers to spend Friday night in Miami, Mitchell called for Saturday's game against the Dallas Mavericks to be postponed. The Cavaliers didn't arrive in Dallas until around noon on Saturday. The starters sat out. Cleveland won the game by 10 against a healthy, playoff-caliber opponent. Tyrese Proctor, Meleek Thomas, Mario Hezonja and Jaylon Tyson all scored between 18 and 24 points.

This wasn't a one-off. Thomas is outscoring Harden and Mobley on a per-minute basis. Proctor is sporting a better-than-6-to-1 assist-to-turnover ratio on the season, and Synergy Sports rates him in the 100th percentile on spot-up efficiency and the 96th in pick-and-rolls, including passes, in terms of points per possession. Tyson breathes life into a transition offense that is otherwise a sore spot. Most of this team's energy comes from the bench.

What exactly the solution here is, we can't say. It will involve a trade. Perhaps a few. But there's something here, and the early indications are that things are going to get better for the team as a whole when it eventually starts leaning on these players a bit more.

Dejounte Murray requested a trade this week. That's not a rumor. The Pelicans publicly acknowledged it and Murray retweeted the news from ESPN. Meanwhile, after Monday's loss to the Golden State Warriors, Jordan Poole was asked if he would ever come back to the team with which he started his career. He answered "yes." Players tend to not be that definitive in those statements, nor do they tend to acknowledge that their former team "just feels like home." It certainly seems as though there's somewhere he'd rather be than New Orleans.

To borrow a phrase from social media user Nathan Calvin, "if you find two ants in your kitchen, the best estimate of the total number of ants in your kitchen is not two." Essentially... if two players seem this eager to flee, more probably do as well. Sam Amick suggested in a radio interview over the summer that Trey Murphy would like to play elsewhere. There has been plenty of speculation about other Pelicans as well. A 4-10 start following 26- and 21-win seasons tends to do that.

We're more than a year into Joe Dumars' reign as head of basketball operations and there's no discernible plan here. Virtually every key player from last year's roster was retained and the team has largely been healthier than it was a year ago, but they're on pace for a worse record under new head coach Jamahl Mosley. The sad thing is that the Pelicans have a fair number of valuable players. They've just assembled those players so carelessly that they've become far less than the sum of their parts. This team is incoherent, and even the players seem to know it.

Trae Young was held scoreless in 26 minutes on Sunday. It was the first time he's been held scoreless in his entire NBA career, but it may be the final straw of a trend that has been bubbling for some time: Trae Young is simply no longer a star-level scorer. He currently has his lowest shooting percentage from both 2-point and 3-point range in a single season. He lacks the burst to get to the rim or beat mismatches consistently anymore, and he's never developed comfort as a catch-and-shooter. Aside from free throws, it's basically all jumpers off the dribble and floaters, neither of which he's making at the rate he needs to in order to justify his defensive shortcomings. He scored 37 points against Detroit last Monday, but needed 17 free throws to get there on less than 35% shooting from the floor. He needs whistles right now.

This is a version of Young who probably shouldn't monopolize an offense, yet he's never shown that he's capable of playing differently. The Wizards are spending 26 possessions a game on shots Young generates either for himself or a teammate out of pick-and-roll, more than any other player in the league, per Synergy Sports. As of Sunday, he and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander were tied for the league lead among starters in average seconds possessing the ball per touch, per NBA.com tracking data. The younger players who represent the future of this organization are spending a whole lot of time watching someone else dribble. Nobody is really spacing the floor for anyone else since there's so little shooting on this roster. The Wizards have played close to neutral when Young rests, but are getting outscored by more than 10 points per 100 possessions with him on the floor. That difference is almost entirely offensive, yet Young remains the same defensive liability he's always been.

This is where the four-year max contract Washington bewilderingly gave Young becomes so destructive. The basic notion of acquiring a high-end point guard to serve as an offensive organizer for these young wings made sense on paper, but they committed to him essentially sight unseen. He played five mostly meaningless games in a tanking season and they paid him max money without really knowing how he'd fit with the team they were building. If he'd walked for nothing in free agency, well, it's not as though they spent picks to get him. Now they're stuck paying star-level money for a non-star-level player who probably can't meaningfully scale down his involvement in the offense because he just doesn't provide much value when any other player on either team has the basketball.

There are a lot of things going wrong in Washington right now, but Young is inevitably going to be the face of those struggles because he's the player the Wizards just bewilderingly gave a four-year max contract to in order to re-sign. Jaylen Brown had the loudest individual loss of the week, but he at least won all of his other games and has largely been what his team has asked him to be. Young went winless this week, had a scoreless game, and maintained his mostly disappointing season-long performance.

If you would have heard "the Warriors have a -2.4 net rating a month into the 2026-27 season," you probably would have shrugged and said, "sure, sounds about right." The Warriors were widely pegged as a low-end Play-In, high-end lottery team before the season, and a -2.4 net rating projects out to a win total in the 30s. Except that isn't Golden State's net rating. It's Golden State's net rating in the minutes Stephen Curry has missed this season.

That's how far above expectations Golden State was playing during its eight-game winning streak. The Curry-off version of the team was around average; the Curry-on version of the team was a juggernaut. The latter feels a bit unsustainable, but we won't know again for around a month. The former is what's about to be tested now that Curry has an oblique abdominal tear. The Spurs hardly represent a fair test for a team in this situation, but San Antonio predictably waxed Golden State by 38 in the first game of Curry's absence.

Nobody's asking for another eight-game winning streak. Those wins are banked, and Golden State's season begins in earnest when Jimmy Butler returns in January or February. For now, the Warriors just need to stay afloat. Find wins where the schedule offers them, and fortunately, the Pelicans, Kings, Clippers and Jazz are on the docket in the next three weeks or so. But losing Curry is a reminder of how fragile that streak really was. Maybe, now that Yaxel Lendeborg is emerging as a possible star, the Warriors are capable of genuine postseason success this season. But the health of any 38-year-old not named LeBron James is going to be precarious. Things could be a lot worse, but Curry's injury drags one of the feel-good stories of the early season back down to Earth.

#2631. Tari Eason gives amazing, blunt explanation for his 25-point game: 'S--t, the Wizards, for real'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night.

While Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season. It was a balanced scoring effort as a team, as six players reached double figures and three scored at least 25 points -- including Tari Eason off the bench.

That 25-point performance represents a new season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench. That effort earned Eason the honor of the walk-off TV interview, during which he gave a brutally honest (and hilarious) answer for why he was able to set a new season high and do so efficiently.

"Shit, the Wizards, for real. It was them," Eason said.

Tari Eason on what allowed him to have a season-high 25 points off the bench tonight:"Shit, the Wizards, for real." pic.twitter.com/t4bOwtzw5r

A+ work here, no notes. Eason could've puffed out his chest after beating up on the Wizards or complimented his teammates for allowing him to get in a rhythm, but instead chose the honest route rarely taken by players in a post-game interview and simply admitted that anyone could get buckets on Washington.

The Wizards are not the worst defense in the NBA -- that honor belongs to the Chicago Bulls -- but they are 25th in defensive rating and certainly do not boast very many elite defenders. Clearly, Eason didn't feel like he was doing anything special or out of the ordinary on Sunday night on his way to 25 points off the bench, and gave credit where it was due to the other team.

Unfortunately for the Wizards, it is not credit they'd like to take, and this feels like the kind of (earned) disrespect that should light some kind of fire under Washington.

#2630. MLB rumors: Blue Jays targeting Ketel Marte, Giants rejecting trade calls for ace Logan Webb

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The annual GM Meetings came and went this week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some sorely needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

Otherwise, the GM Meetings brought a lot of rumors and presumably the groundwork was laid for moves that could be completed later this offseason. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

The Blue Jays have interest in Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte, who has a full no-trade protection, reports Sportsnet. It does not appear a trade is imminent. We ranked Marte among the offseason's top trade candidates despite his odd AWOL incidents the last few seasons. Even at 33, he remains one of the game's best second basemen.

The Blue Jays went 79-83 this past season largely because of their offense, which ranked dead last in runs and home runs. They also ranked 17th in WAR at second base as All-Star Ernie Clement ran out of steam in the second half. Offensively, Marte is coming off his worst 162-game season since 2018, though he would still represent a clear upgrade for the Blue Jays.

The Giants continue to decline trade calls about ace righty Logan Webb, reports USA Today. Webb, 30 next week, had his worst full season in the big leagues in 2026, in part due to a nagging knee injury, though he is signed affordably through 2028. San Francisco needs to add to its rotation, not subtract one of the game's best and most durable starters.

That said, a Webb trade would presumably net the Giants multiple young players and improve the team's talent base. It never hurts to listen, but for now, the Giants seem disinclined to move their best pitcher since Madison Bumgarner was in his prime. Webb and Landen Roupp are the only locks for San Francisco's 2027 rotation at the moment.

Not surprisingly, the Braves want to add at least one starting pitcher, according to The Athletic. They could also re-sign Raisel Iglesias or bring in another late-inning reliever even after signing Phillips. Chris Sale and Grant Holmes are Atlanta's only returning healthy starters. Bryce Elder (knee), Spencer Schwellenbach (elbow) and Spencer Strider (elbow) all finished the season injured.

The Braves will give Didier Fuentes, who was so dominant as a reliever this past season, a chance to start in 2027. It will be difficult to count on him for a full season, however. Fuentes, 21, threw a career-high 97 innings between the minors, majors, and postseason in 2026. Atlanta will need to monitor his workload next year. Another starter to soak up innings is a must this offseason.

The Tigers have interest in free agent left-hander Shota Imanaga, reports MLB.com. Jackson Jobe, Troy Melton, River Ryan, and Framber Valdez are presumably locks for Detroit's rotation. Ty Madden and Keider Montero are depth options. Reese Olson is expected back from shoulder surgery early next year. Still, the Tigers could clearly use another starting pitcher.

We ranked Imanaga, 33, as the 30th-best free agent available this offseason. He has been very home run prone the last two years (1.9 homers per nine innings), which could make him a good match for what is now called Fifth Third Park. Detroit's stadium tends to play pitcher-friendly, particularly in April and September (and October), when the ball doesn't carry well in the cold.

The Blue Jays are receiving calls about infielder Ernie Clement and utility man Davis Schneider, reports The Athletic. Teams have also inquired about catcher Brandon Valenzuela, who was a Gold Glove finalist as a rookie in 2026. Toronto reportedly has interest in Jazz Chisholm Jr. as it seeks more of a power bat on the infield, potentially making Clement expendable.

Schneider, 27, had a poor 2026 and spent time in Triple-A, though he is versatile and has hit lefties in spots over the years. There is a shocking shortage of quality right-handed bats throughout baseball right now. Schneider's heavy plate discipline approach and ability to play left field as well as some infield positions make him an interesting enough target this offseason.

The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox are among several teams pursuing Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Taira, 26, had a 1.36 ERA in 145 innings for the Seibu Lions in 2026. We ranked him as the 19th-best free agent available this offseason, though he could ultimately wind up in the bullpen given his height (5-foot-8).

The Padres and two Chicago teams need starting pitching this offseason (they need multiple starters, really) and would likely use Taira in their rotation, at least to begin the season. For what it's worth, Taira told Sanspo he does not have a preferred destination, geographically. The Cubs, Padres, and White Sox would all give him a chance to pitch for a contender right away.

The Cardinals have declined trade inquiries into first baseman Alec Burleson and shortstop Masyn Winn, according to the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. St. Louis is also receiving interest in catchers Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés, who are more likely to be traded. Burleson and Winn are off-limits, though, and considered part of the long-term future in St. Louis.

Leo Bernal, who was so impressive during his September call up, and top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez are the future behind the plate for the Cardinals. Pagés is a traditional glove-first backup catcher. Crooks has some offensive upside thanks to his hard-hit ability (exit velocity, etc.), and he rates well as a pitch-framer and thrower. He's an appealing target for catcher-needy teams.
